title: A Powdered Sugar Mustache
summary: Grandma Rivka is making Hanukkah doughnuts, and every grandchild wants a different filling: Noam wants chocolate, Leah wants jam, and little Tali wants... ketchup! And Grandpa? Salted fish! After every bite: "Big bite, sugar flies, POOF! and a white mustache!" Only Grandma doesn't eat sweets. Or does she? A sweet, funny rhyming story about a grandma, her grandkids and doughnuts.
pages:
Grandma Rivka tied her kerchief and her flowered apron, too,
and poured flour in a great big bowl: "Who wants doughnuts? Grandkids — you?"
Noam jumped, and Leah jumped, and little Tali, smallest of all:
"Me! Me! Me!" — and the cat just yawned and fell asleep on the old sofa by the wall.

Grandma kneaded, and the dough puffed up, and rose, and grew,
till it peeked out of the bowl — round and plump, like a big hill, too.
Then Grandma fried them — tssss! — golden balls in oil so hot,
and the smell flew out the window, down the street and the next — and reached the whole lot!

Noam said, "Mine with chocolate! Chocolate warm and sweet!"
Grandma filled it — SQUIRT! — Noam said the blessing, then took a giant, deep bite to eat.
Big bite, sugar flies — POOF! — and a white mustache!

Leah said, "I want mine with jam! Red jam, as sweet as can be!"
She bit — SQUIRT! — jam on her nose, and her cheek, and her green shirt, see!
Big bite, sugar flies — POOF! — and a white mustache!

And little Tali shouted, "And I want mine — with ketchup!" — "What?! Ketchup?! With sugar on top?!"
Grandma laughed and filled it — and Tali bit: "Mmm! Another one! And more tomorrow — don't stop!"
Big bite, sugar flies — POOF! — and a white mustache!

And Grandpa stroked his beard, straightened his hat, and whispered, "And I'd like mine... with salted fish."
"With FISH?!" everyone shouted. And Grandma rolled her eyes: "Oh, all right... but eat it outside, in the wind, if you wish!"

A bite, and a bite, and another bite — and powdered sugar flew like snow all over the place,
on the table, on the chairs, and on the cat — who woke up and sneezed: "Achoo! What did you do to my face?"
Noam — a mustache! Leah — a mustache! And Tali — a mustache up to her ears!
And Grandpa? His white beard is now white... times two, it appears!

Only Grandma stood aside — all clean, with her ironed apron and glasses on her nose:
"Me? No, no. Grandma doesn't eat sweets. I just serve, and wipe the hands, and that's how it goes."

"Come on, Grandma! Just one bite!" — "Well... just a crumb. One tiny crumb, my friend..."
Big bite, sugar flies — POOF! — and a white mustache!
And her glasses — white! And her nose — white! And Grandma's mustache? The biggest of all! Curled like a captain's at each end!

By the window the menorah glowed, and everyone sang "Maoz Tzur" with cheer,
with a white mustache under each nose — the whole family here.
And Grandma tied her apron again: "Well... who wants more doughnuts? Grandkids — you?"
"Me! Me! Me!" — and POOF! — another white cloud... and more mustaches, too.
